title: ZotFlag
text:
ZotFlag infographic


It is a Zotero extension (for Zotero 7 to 10) that automatically adds tags to selected references when their metadata matches lists kept in CSV files.

GitHub Repository
Discussion, application and empirical analysis (in French).








CSV filenames
Matching Zotero fields




keywords.csv
Tags (strict equality)
Title (whole word or phrase)
Abstract (whole word or phrase)


journals.csv
Publication title (journal, book, proceedings, website…) and journal abbreviation
ISSN


persons.csv
All creators (author, editor, other roles), target in Last Name, First Name format


publishers.csv
Publisher (and equivalent fields: university, institution, label…)


dois.csv
DOI field
DOI: line in the Extra field
doi.org in URL field


urls.csv
URL



Usage : Right-click + ZotFlag. Or F12 keyboard shortcut (to index all).
Language : The interface (menu, messages, settings, template files) follows the language selected in Zotero: English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), Dutch, Japanese, Simplified Chinese. For any other language, ZotFlag is displayed in English (or in the closest variant). To add a language: copy locale/en-US/zotflag.ftl to locale/<code>/ and translate it.
Columns : TagsToAdd/, LookingFor, and any other column (e.g., Notes) ignored. One line = one tag for one target; repeat the line for multiple tags or multiple variants. Non case sensitive. No accent sensitive. No truncation/ No wildcard.

Matching Rules (Strict Only)

No truncation, no automatic variants: create one line per variant yourself.
Ignored: case, accents and ligatures (é = e, ç = c, œ = oe), multiple spaces, typographic apostrophes/hyphens, HTML tags like <i>, etc.
Persons: Roux, D matches Roux D (and “Roux D.”) but not Roux Damien. A target without a comma matches a name in a single field (institution).
keywords.csv: The term must appear as a whole word/phrase (“jeu de rôle” does not match “jeux de rôle” nor “jeu de rôles”). A target that is an existing tag (e.g., _jeu de rôle) allows adding a generic tag (e.g., _JEU); additions can chain together (multiple levels possible).
An already existing tag is never duplicated. Read-only libraries are ignored.
Comma, semicolon, or tab separator detected automatically; UTF-8 (fallback Windows-1252).

GPL-3.0-or-later. Author: Pascal Martinolli (specifications); code generated with Claude.

« Make it so. » was a catchphrase written by Gene Roddenberry, inspired by the British naval officers of the XIXe century. It was first used in “Encounter At Farpoint” (28 September 1987) and then reused with much delight by Captain Jean-Luc Picard (In memoriam) during the run of ST:TNG 1987-1994.
